negative_findings.description: No dedicated, structured registry of vendor-announced private-sector contract wins in Hungary exists; there is no Hungarian equivalent of a commercial 'deal tracker' covering bank/retail technology awards.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in both hu and en returned only scattered vendor newsrooms and trade-press articles; no aggregator scoped to Hungary.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be vendor-by-vendor (many small crawls) rather than one high-yield feed, raising ongoing cost and increasing miss risk.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language queries built on 'sajtóközlemény' + 'szállító' + 'bank' surfaced mostly banking-association and central-bank press pages, not vendor win announcements.
negative_findings.result_summary: Top HU results were bankszovetseg.hu and mnb.hu press rooms plus academic history material — off-cell for vendor announcements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hungarian vendors appear to publish wins under 'referencia'/'esettanulmány'/'ügyfeleink' rather than 'sajtóközlemény'; query vocabulary must be adjusted to those terms.

negative_findings.description: No Hungary-specific card-issuing/processing vendor win announcement was located for 2025-2026 despite targeted search (issuer-processor space).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned generic issuer-processor marketing pages and non-Hungarian partnerships only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card issuing/processing is a core Printec-adjacent segment; absence of evidence here is a discovery gap, not evidence of no deals.

negative_findings.description: Vendor newsroom URLs for NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Intellect Design, GK Software and Barion were inferred from the vendor's known site structure rather than opened during this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Not fetched in this run; liveness unknown.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These need the deterministic verification pass; do not treat the URL paths as confirmed.

coverage_gaps.description: Fraud/AML and open-banking vendor announcements touching Hungarian banks (e.g. NICE Actimize, BioCatch, Featurespace, Tink/Salt Edge-class providers) were not surfaced.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run per-vendor site-restricted searches ('site:vendor.com Hungary|Magyar|OTP|MBH|K&H|Erste|CIB|Raiffeisen') across a named fraud/open-banking vendor list.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian bank actor names were not yet used systematically as search anchors against vendor sites (MBH Bank, OTP, K&H, Erste Hungary, CIB, Raiffeisen, UniCredit Hungary, Gránit, MagNet, Takarékbank legacy).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a bank actor list with aliases/legacy names (Budapest Bank, MKB, Takarék → MBH) and re-query each vendor newsroom by bank name in hu and en.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language search used 'sajtóközlemény/szállító/szerződés' but not the reference-page vocabulary that actually carries Hungarian vendor wins.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run HU queries with 'referenciáink', 'esettanulmány', 'ügyfeleink', 'sikertörténet', 'bevezetés', 'élesítés', 'partnerünk', plus 'közbeszerzési eljárás nyertese'.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor LinkedIn pages, conference/awards submissions and annual-report customer lists — often the only place a Hungarian win is named — were not covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add LinkedIn company-post monitoring (ToS-compliant), vendor annual reports, and industry award shortlists (Global Banking & Finance, IBS, Efma) as a secondary discovery channel.

coverage_gaps.description: Retail (non-bank) side of the cell is thin — only one POS vendor (GK via Lidl) surfaced; Hungarian retailer self-checkout, payment terminal and loyalty vendor wins remain uncovered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query retail-tech vendors (Toshiba Global Commerce, Zebra, Ingenico, Worldline, Nexi, PAX, SPS/Sonepar-class integrators) plus Hungarian retail trade press (Trade magazin, Piac & Profit) in Hungarian.

brief: For Hungarian bank and retailer technology deals, the seller is almost always the discloser: private-sector awards surface in vendor newsrooms (Tietoevry, Oracle, Intellect/iGCB, Euronet, Diebold Nixdorf, GK), in vendor customer-reference libraries (Asseco Case Study Book, Comarch, Broadcom PDF case studies), and in Hungarian-language 'referenciáink'/blog pages of domestic suppliers (4iG, DSS Consulting, Mindspire, Smartsector). There is no Hungary-scoped aggregator of such announcements, so coverage must be assembled vendor-by-vendor and swept via pointer feeds (FinTech Futures Hungary keyword page, IBS Intelligence, Financial IT, The Paypers, ATM Marketplace, Bitport.hu). Hungarian-language yield was materially lower than English because local vendors publish wins under reference/case-study vocabulary rather than 'sajtóközlemény'; the query set must be rebuilt around 'referenciáink', 'esettanulmány', 'ügyfeleink' and Hungarian bank aliases (MKB/Budapest Bank/Takarék → MBH). Biggest remaining holes are fraud/AML and open-banking vendors, and the retailer-side POS/self-checkout vendor landscape.
